extracted.intended_audience: educated readers, scholars, and statesmen (early-modern/General audience interested in philosophy of learning)
extracted.subtask_description: Extracted evaluative principles and prescriptive criteria from Francis Bacon's 'The Advancement of Learning' (First Book): standards about the purpose, limits, methods, and social uses of knowledge and learning. Aimed at guiding rulers, scholars, and inquirers toward productive study and reform of the sciences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge's true end is 'the glory of the Creator and the relief of man's estate.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bacon states that the highest purpose of study is not personal aggrandizement, disputation, or profit, but service: to glorify God and to relieve human life. Usefulness and moral/dious ends are primary evaluative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject learning for pride, ostentation, or commerce
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning should not be sought merely as 'a couch... a terrace... a tower of state... a fort... or a shop for profit or sale'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Anti-patterns include treating learning as social ornament, status display, or commodity. Assess works by whether they aim at genuine understanding and public benefit rather than vanity or gain.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three limitations on the pursuit of knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning must be bounded by three cautions: (1) do not place felicity in knowledge so as to forget mortality; (2) apply knowledge so it gives repose not disquiet; (3) do not presume to attain the mysteries of God by natural inquiry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are normative constraints on both the scope and the application of inquiry. They guide what is appropriate to pursue, how to present conclusions, and when to abstain from overreaching metaphysical claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Charity (moral end) must temper knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge without charity inflates: 'Scientia inflat' — 'Knowledge bloweth up, but charity buildeth up.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate research or learning projects by their relation to humane ends; knowledge divorced from benevolent purpose is judged negatively. Bacon emphasizes that moral disposition is part of quality assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Usefulness and application as a criterion
rubrics_metrics.description: Knowledge should be applied and bring 'relief of man's estate' — learning must lead to works or practical benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bacon criticizes purely speculative or disputatious learning; when judging intellectual work, prefer approaches that show potential for concrete application or improvement of life and society.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid pure disputation and unfruitful methods
rubrics_metrics.description: The old logic/Organon and disputative methods are 'unfruitful' if they produce only argument rather than works that benefit life.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Methodological criteria: prefer inquiry methods that generate new results, experiments, inventions, or applicable knowledge rather than mere rhetorical victory or scholastic hairsplitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Universality of learning (divine and human)
rubrics_metrics.description: Learning ought to be both 'divine and human'—comprehensive across sacred and profane studies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bacon values a broad map of knowledge: evaluation should consider whether a program or work engages relevant domains (natural, moral, theological) appropriately and comprehensively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Survey and map neglected subjects ('fresh and waste')
rubrics_metrics.description: The practical aim is 'a general and faithful perambulation of learning, with an inquiry what parts thereof lie fresh and waste' — identify unexploited fields ripe for improvement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A criterion for scholarly agendas: prioritize research that documents gaps and converts neglected areas into productive inquiry; prefer planned, strategic cultivation of overlooked topics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinguish demonstrative from conjectural knowledge
rubrics_metrics.description: In matters of policy and governance, learning must teach 'what things are in their nature demonstrative, and what are conjectural', and how to use distinctions and exceptions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess arguments and methods by whether authors correctly mark degrees of certainty, avoid overclaiming, and show sound judgment about when to resolve and when to suspend judgment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Historical and example-based instruction for practical judgment
rubrics_metrics.description: Reading the errors and examples of past statesmen and rulers provides corrective lessons: 'let him look into the errors of Clement VII... and he will fly apace from being irresolute.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate case-based scholarship on its capacity to produce transferable practical wisdom. Use historical exemplars as tests and corrective tools for contemporary decision-making.

rubrics_metrics.name: Learning strengthens governance and arms (not weakens)
rubrics_metrics.description: Counter to critics, learning can coexist with military and political prowess; ages have combined both.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating whether education harms action, require evidence; Bacon uses historical concurrence to show that learned states often excel. Criteria: does learning enrich policy-making capacities rather than produce mere dilettantism?

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer learned (theoretical) grounding over mere empiricism in practitioners
rubrics_metrics.description: Relying solely on empiric practitioners (those of practice without books) is risky; learned practitioners understand causes and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In professional evaluation, value integration of practice and deep theoretical understanding rather than mere rote recipes or narrow expedients.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid unwisely mixing theological and natural inquiries
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not 'unwisely mingle or confound' divine learning with natural philosophy—each has proper bounds; natural inquiry cannot settle mysteries of God.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion for appropriateness: respect disciplinary boundaries and do not claim metaphysical conclusions from natural science; maintain methodological humility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote continual progress and proficience in learning
rubrics_metrics.description: Men should 'endeavour an endless progress or proficience' in both Scripture and nature rather than accepting premature limits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate research programs for commitment to cumulative advancement and sustained effort rather than satisfaction with minor or purely decorative contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fill leisure with study that strengthens action
rubrics_metrics.description: Leisure of active men should be filled with studies that preserve the mind against idleness and prepare for business ('no man need doubt that learning will expel business, but rather it will keep and defend the possession of the mind against idleness and pleasure').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess personal scholarly habits and curricula for their capacity to sustain resilience, practical readiness, and disciplined thought in public life.
